title: Comment on: “Timing of arthrocentesis and its association with treatment success in painful temporomandibular joint disorders: a two-decade cohort study”
html: We have read with great enthusiasm the work by Tang et al.1, who provide compelling evidence that a longer symptom duration prior to initial arthrocentesis is significantly associated with lower odds of patient-reported treatment success (OR 0.974 per month; 95% CI 0.966–0.983), and that performing arthrocentesis within 6 months of symptom onset improves odds of success nearly threefold (OR 2.71). These findings usefully support earlier intervention for refractory intra-articular pathology.
